### Exercise 15.8: Find angle sizes where there are two transversals

1. In the diagram below, $EF \parallel GH$; $JK$ is a transversal and $LM$ is a transversal. Determine the sizes of $a$ and $b$, giving reasons for your answers.

Image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-0_057.png
records.answer_text:
Concentrate on $a$ first.

Highlighted image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-1_008.png

$EF \parallel GH$, and $a$ is alternate to the angle marked $80^{\circ}$.

$$
\begin{align}
a = 80^{\circ} \quad\left( \text{alt }\angle\text{s; }EF \parallel GH \right) \\
\end{align}
$$

($a$ is not equal to $65^{\circ}$, because $JK$ and $LM$ are not parallel.)

Now determine the size of $b$.

$EF \parallel GH$, and $b$ and the angle marked $65^{\circ}$ are co-interior angles.

Highlighted image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-2_007.png

$$
\begin{align}
b + 65^{\circ} & = 180^{\circ} \left( \text{co-int }\angle\text{s; }EF \parallel GH \right) \\
b & = 180^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} \\
b & = 115^{\circ} \\
\end{align}
$$

(Because $JK$ and $LM$ are not parallel, $b$ is not equal to $100^{\circ}$.)

In the diagram below, $ML \parallel JK$ and $PQ$ is a transversal. Determine the value of $s$. Give reasons for all your statements.

Image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-0_037.png
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Consider the diagram and plan how you will get to the answer. We cannot determine the value of $s$ in just one step. It is a good idea to begin with the angle that is given.

Step 2: Choose another angle that is closer to $s$ and has a relationship to the angle you need to find.

$ML \parallel JK$ so we can use the F-U-N angles. We can see that $K \hat{R} S$ is alternate to the $65^{\circ}$ angle.

Step 3: Find the size of the other angle.

$$
\begin{align}
 K\hat{R}S & = 65^{\circ} \quad(\text{alt }\angle\text{s; }JK \parallel LM) \\
 \end{align}
$$

Highlighted image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-1_033.png

Step 4: Determine the value of $s$.

Now that we know the size of $K\hat{R}S$, we can determine $s$. We can see that $s$ and $K\hat{R}S$ are angles on a straight line.

Highlighted image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-2_008.png

$$
\begin{align}
 s + 65^{\circ} & = 180^{\circ} \quad(\text{adj }\angle\text{s on str line}) \\
 s & = 180^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} \\
 \therefore s & = 115^{\circ} \\
 \end{align}
$$
